topic: Parameterized-complexity frontier for latent-K Gaussian innovation-variance fibers. Input a rational positive-definite covariance faithful to an undirected no-collider forest and K; define each component-root signature by its exact Gaussian regression residual variances. Completely classify whether a root tuple with at most K distinct labels exists, conjecturally by a faithful rational W[1]-hardness reduction with a linear-K ETH lower bound, while accepting a twin-star-resistant f(K) polynomial algorithm if that is the correct answer. Extend the classification to uniqueness and two-witness recovery. For a supplied component order, prove the exact (K+1)2^q polynomial DP and a matching q lower bound, where q is the maximum set of labels recurring across a cut. Use Gaussian covariance-confidence-region projection for orientation and total-effect inference. Consumer: SEMgraph's bottom-up equal-error-variance mode. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived root-union and root-locus characterizations, polynomial dictionary verification, a d^K polynomial algorithm when components have size at most d, and a faithful independent two-node covariance block whose identical two-root signature transfers nonemptiness to two-witness recovery while preserving q. The ordered q-DP matched exhaustive enumeration on 83 forests and 14,800 budget/order checks. Destructive work confirmed that common-center star set-cover gadgets have a cheap universal witness, varying centers introduces costly complementary labels, and Gaussian signatures obey product and rational-square constraints; no collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Build a faithful rational Gaussian selector-and-compatibility realization with linear parameter budget and no unintended internal-root witnesses, or derive a symbolic K-FPT invariant that avoids such a reduction. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively enumerate one three-choice selector and one compatibility gadget, verifying exact intended root tuples, rational positive-definite faithful covariance, and bounded auxiliary-label cost; any cheap unintended witness kills that reduction template. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_latentk_variance_fiber.md

open_problems.why_unsolved: The causal literature fixes either one common variance or a known equality partition, whereas this problem existentially chooses component roots and thereby induces an unknown equality pattern under a global K-label budget. Prior CausalSmith work explicitly excluded vertex-coloured innovation variances, and its fan-in frontier showed that a superficially small structural parameter can remain zero on a hard family. Generic minimum-label hardness does not transfer automatically: selector and compatibility labels must be realized as exact Schur-complement residual variances of one rational positive-definite covariance while preserving forest faithfulness and excluding unintended root witnesses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A dichotomy theorem giving either an f(K)poly(n,L) decision-and-witness algorithm or a faithful rational reduction with K'=O(k) proving W[1]/W[2]-hardness and excluding f(K)n^{o(K)} time under ETH.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing colored-DAG geometry begins with a fixed coloring and studies its covariance image; the inverse problem here prescribes exact collisions and separations among all possible component-root signatures. Prior sparse rational separators and private-slot compilers do not control equality classes across alternative forest roots. The first proof step that changes is the gadget soundness lemma: every feasible root must encode one intended selector choice, each incompatibility must consume a provably new label, and positive definiteness, faithfulness, rational bit complexity, product or rational-square constraints, and absence of unintended internal-root collisions must hold simultaneously. A failure of this inverse realization step could instead expose a symbolic invariant forcing K-FPT behavior.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic realization theorem with rational bit-complexity and compositional gadget bounds, or a forbidden-pattern invariant together with an explicit smallest nonrealizable selector-and-compatibility incidence system.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Subset-state lower-bound technology exists, but q is not ordinary graph pathwidth: its boundary objects are exact numerical variance labels that may disappear and recur across ordered components. Prior LiMVAM work quotiented prefixes by removed sets and proved suffix legality depended only on that state, but retained all 2^p subsets. Here the missing upper-bound step is a right-congruence theorem proving that the capped number of completed labels plus the subset of q live recurring labels is sufficient. A matching lower bound must realize 2^q distinguishable live-label obligations through faithful rational Gaussian signatures without artificially increasing K or q.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correctness theorem for a DP with at most (K+1)2^q states per cut, polynomial-time exact-arithmetic transitions and witness backpointers, paired with a q-preserving reduction excluding (2-epsilon)^q poly(n,K,L) time under SETH or primal-pathwidth SETH.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Unconstrained source-forest multiplicity factors over independent root choices, but an at-most-K equality budget couples components globally. Generic second-solution theory also warns that decision, uniqueness, and another-witness recovery need not share a complexity classification unless reductions preserve solutions. In this fiber, different structural roots may induce identical numerical signatures, and mere label renaming must not manufacture a second witness. The missing proof step is therefore a canonical witness equivalence together with either a parsimonious Gaussian reduction or a self-reduction that excludes one canonical tuple without increasing K or the supplied-order width q.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem classifying UNIQUE-FIBER and SECOND-FIBER as FPT, XP, or parameterized-hard, with an algorithm returning two canonically distinct root tuples when they exist and determining whether they induce distinct total-effect functionals.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The at-most-K model is a nonregular union over root tuples and latent equality partitions, with intersections where labels merge and faithfulness boundaries where orientations become unstable. Existing work treats all-equal errors or confidence sets over candidate orderings, not projection through a budgeted equality fiber. Prior CausalSmith outward inversion remained set-theoretic rather than executable, and the closest blocked-Gaussian run failed at noncompact image geometry and comparison-parameter elimination. The missing first step is a computable membership inversion over a covariance confidence region that retains every equality and singular branch before projecting accepted models through rational total-effect maps.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A covariance-region projection algorithm whose orientation set and total-effect image have finite-sample or uniformly asymptotic 1-alpha joint coverage over the K-label forest model, with regular-stratum shrinking, explicit singular-collision fallback, and a polynomial, FPT-in-K, or 2^q computational guarantee.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates effect inference that retains causal-structure uncertainty and separates structural from numerical uncertainty.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A learned graph is uncertain -> treating it as fixed produces overconfident effect intervals -> test inversion propagates every compatible structure -> latent K-label fibers require the same propagation over unknown variance groupings

method_exemplars.technique: Use split likelihood ratios and Markov-inequality calibration to obtain finite-sample coverage without regular likelihood-ratio asymptotics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The K-label covariance fiber is nonregular at merging labels and intersecting root models, where universal inference can avoid an intractable limiting law.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt union-null test inversion and constrained Gaussian likelihood optimization, then project accepted covariance-root pairs to total-effect values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves structure-aware total-effect coverage at K=1; the new work replaces that stratum by the at-most-K union.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests and projection of an ordering confidence set to ancestral relations and causal-effect intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its output is the same set-valued orientation and effect statement, but candidate orderings must additionally carry latent-label feasibility.

literature_map:
Peters and Bühlmann (2014, Biometrika) prove full Gaussian DAG identifiability at the all-equal K=1 endpoint.
Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019, Biometrika; arXiv:1807.03419) turn equal variance into conditional-variance orderings and scalable top-down and bottom-up algorithms.
Wu and Drton (2023, IEEE JSAIT; arXiv:2308.08959) characterize partial homoscedasticity when the equal-variance partition is given, leaving latent partition selection outside their model.
Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2404.04024) develop colored Gaussian DAG geometry, rational-identification tools, and faithfulness results for fixed colorings, but not inverse root-signature realization.
Jakobsen, Shah, Bühlmann, and Peters (2022, JMLR; arXiv:2108.08871) give polynomial directed-tree optimization, identifiability-gap analysis, and post-selection substructure tests, but not K-budgeted innovation labels.
Gao, Ding, and Aragam (2022, AISTATS; arXiv:2201.10548) derive minimax-optimal Gaussian DAG recovery from conditional-variance concentration under equal variances, providing a nearby estimation rung.
Recent equal-variance work by Daskalakis, Kandiros, and Yao (2025; arXiv:2511.06164) sharpens sample complexity while remaining at K=1.
Fellows, Guo, and Kanj (2010, JCSS) show W[2]-hardness for generic minimum-label graph problems even at small pathwidth, suggesting hardness without providing Gaussian-realizable gadgets.
Marx (2010, Theory of Computing) supplies CSP and treewidth algorithms with matching ETH-style lower-bound machinery for choice variables with large domains.
Lampis (2025, SODA; arXiv:2403.07239) gives tight base-two barriers for subset-state dynamic programs over linear interfaces, relevant to recurring labels across supplied-order cuts.
Yato and Seta (2003, IEICE) and Creignou et al. (2013; arXiv:1309.5009) separate decision from second-solution recovery and supply solution-preserving and parameterized-enumeration machinery.
Strieder and Drton (2023, Journal of Causal Inference; arXiv:2309.04298) invert tests for total effects under equal-variance structure uncertainty and motivate extensions to other model assumptions.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026, JASA; arXiv:2305.14506) construct confidence sets for causal orderings and project them to ancestral and effect statements.
Searches for unknown partial-homoscedastic partitions, K distinct innovation variances, faithful Gaussian forest gadgets, recurring-label width, and second root tuples found no paper occupying the latent-K complexity, inverse-realization, q-frontier, uniqueness, or uncertainty-projection targets.
